chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn al-Fadl al-Wasiti, who said:

I wrote to Al-Rida (peace be upon him): A man divorced his wife with the divorce by which she is not permissible to him until she marries another husband, and a boy who had not reached puberty married her. He (AS) said: No, until he reaches puberty. And I wrote to him: What is the limit of puberty? He (AS) said: That which imposes the obligations (of hudud/punishments) upon the believer.

key_terms.الرُّضَا ع: Al-Rida (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Ali al-Rida
key_terms.الطَّلَاقِ الَّذِي لَا تَحِلُّ لَهُ حَتَ: The divorce by which she is not permissible to him until she marries another (three divorces)
key_terms.لَمْ يَحْتَلِم: Did not reach puberty / did not experience seminal emission

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of puberty in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that in a 'three divorce' scenario, a boy's marriage to the woman is valid but suspended until he reaches puberty, defined functionally as the onset of *hudud* (legal punishments). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on *bulugh* (puberty) as the threshold for full legal accountability (*taklif*), distinguishing it from mere physical maturity. The reference to *hudud* underscores the transition from childhood to adulthood in Islamic law, where the individual becomes liable for religious and legal obligations.
